note:
The routing RECORD as it rides on kind:44221 `session.create` and on the seat's kind:44223 metadata. Brian's ruling of 2026-08-30.

The record is the ANSWER. Only the founder's host writes it, because only the host can see its own live kind:44222 catalog. It is the counterpart of testdata/routing/hire-request-fixture.json, and the three records here answer the three requests there.

THE RULE: thirteen keys, always, `null` where the answer is genuinely absent - a strict observer has exactly one shape to accept. `risk` carries FOUR keys here (the three factors plus their product `score`, which the validator checks against the factors). `reviewRequired` may not be false while `reviewReasons` names triggers that fired. `chosen.effort` may only be low, medium or high: xhigh, max and ultra are human override only. The fourteenth key, `proposedDisagreement`, is written ONLY when the host's own choice differs from the `proposed` the hire carried - so a record with nothing to disclose stays byte-identical to the thirteen-key form.

Pinned by buzz-core (crates/buzz-core/src/coding_session_routing.rs, RoutingRecord), the CLI (crates/buzz-cli/src/commands/sessions/route.rs) and the desktop (desktop/src/features/coding-sessions/lib/codingSessionRoutingRecord.ts).

records.name: fast builder - the host agreed with what the hire proposed
records.why: Answers request 1. The host routed for itself and landed on the same target the requester proposed, so `proposedDisagreement` is absent entirely and this is the plain thirteen-key shape.

routing.reason: codex-primary/gpt-5.6-luna cleared the builder gate (agency>=4.4, coding>=4.2, discipline>=4.5, verification>=4.2) and is the cheapest expected accepted completion at fast/low (2.0 vs 2.5 for codex-primary/gpt-5.4-mini)

records.name: standard builder run on the human's override
records.why: Answers request 2. The override is honoured, so `chosen` is the human's target and the router's own pick survives as `runnerUp` rather than disappearing. No `proposedDisagreement`: the difference from `proposed` is the requester's own instruction, not the host's judgment, and reporting it would be a disagreement nobody had.

routing.reason: human override: spending this lane's standard builder job on Terra deliberately: it is a challenger for this class (spec 8) and has no measured result yet, and this lane is reversible enough to be the place to buy one

override.because: spending this lane's standard builder job on Terra deliberately: it is a challenger for this class (spec 8) and has no measured result yet, and this lane is reversible enough to be the place to buy one

records.name: deep architect where the host overruled the proposal, and said so
records.why: Answers request 3, for a requester that did propose something. Review is required and the four spec 6 triggers are listed in spec order, so `reviewRequired` may not be false. The host's own catalog put codex-primary/gpt-5.6-sol ahead of the claude-primary/opus[1m] the requester proposed, and `proposedDisagreement` is the host saying that out loud - a silent divergence would leave a lead reading its own proposal back as though it had been honoured.

routing.reason: codex-primary/gpt-5.6-sol cleared the architect gate (context>=4.5, discipline>=4.5, judgment>=4.7, reasoning>=4.7, verification>=4.5) and is the cheapest expected accepted completion at deep/high (5.0 vs 5.6 for claude-primary/opus[1m])
routing.proposedDisagreement: the requester proposed claude-primary/opus[1m] (high); this host routed codex-primary/gpt-5.6-sol[high] (high) against its own live catalog and registry, and the host's decision is the one that ran

rejected.name: the request shape on a create
rejected.why: The mirror of the hire fixture's rejected case. A create that carried only the question would claim a decision nobody made; the validator must refuse it and name the key that does not belong.

rejected.name: a score that contradicts its own factors
rejected.why: 3x3x2 is 18, not 19. A record that can lie about its own arithmetic can lie about anything downstream of it.
